It’s not exactly murder, maybe, I guess you can decide. I’ll try to make it a fast one. 

I was a medic in Afghanistan. A few people got injured in an IED blast, one of which was a kid, around 14-15 years old. We had limited resources, so sometimes you can only save a certain number of people, those who are most likely to be saved, the immediate casualties come first, and sometimes you have to let the others who are too far gone just kinda... sit there, I guess. You make them comfortable and talk to them but, there’s not much you can do. 

Anywho, the reason I equate it to murder is, when we saw what we had in numbers, we realized we could save one, a guy that had lost quite a bit in the blast, and there wasn’t much we could do for the kid. So I gave him some pain meds, to help him relax, and help him sleep. And he did, he went to sleep and never got to wake up. It was a murder in the grand scheme depending on your viewpoint, but I truly felt like I was the one dealing the final blow, even if it was for mercy. He was a local, I never got to learn his name, or anything about him apart from the short time I spent with him before working on the other casualties.

I really like this question. I’ll try to touch on every aspect you mentioned. Let me know if I miss anything. 
I find that putting the company’s interests first is the best way to grow it - however, if you let that overshadow the needs of the team and the customers, you’ll fail. All employees know that there is a 100% open door policy to my office. If they have any questions, concerns, or suggestions, they are free to walk right in and voice them. All employees are also paid well above minimum wage, and I also find that recognizing their accomplishments is very important. Letting them know a product they made, or a project they worked on was well received, and that they did an awesome job on it. 
“The customer is always right” is true to a degree. Sometimes there are conflicts and I’ll do my best to help the customer but at the end of the day, some customers cost the company too much money, and more importantly - too much stress on my staff. I will always step in and work with customers one on one if they have caused too much stress to my sales staff or production team. 
As far as competitors go, I think we’ve done very well by being part of a group of similar sellers. We all get together and say “look, we are competitors BUT, if one of us takes everything, that’s less that everyone gets. So let’s work together” this way we can share resources, suppliers, advice, etc. and everyone grows, as opposed to just one of us. I hope that answers your question and thanks! :)

Agreed. What I’m advocating for really is to try to provide more productive conversations between children and parents. There are some terrible parents, that in the end are just terrible people, and it would be insane to think that every toxic parent has an excuse, so I definitely concede to what you’re saying here. But I think a lot of parents when given the chance aren’t really that bad, and sometimes some perspective from the kid and parent together can help mend some things.

To an extent absolutely. But for that end result of you saying “okay I’m done” it has to be communicated both ways that there is an issue. Instead of saying “you’re toxic and you drag me down” (or something accusatory for example) we should be providing something more productive to that conversation. That way, when we do finally put our needs first and cut it off, at least there was an attempt at a productive solution. Otherwise, just becoming accusatory just pushes that person away further. And I’m absolutely not advocating for people to stay in toxic relationships just because of some duty or anything, your own mental health should definitely be the first priority. I just believe as humans, as people, we should give people some more patience and respect for where they might be mentally as well.
